description.p: Ferramari is a video wallpaper for Linux, written in Rust. 🦀

Play local videos, streaming URLs or web pages as your desktop wallpaper, one source per monitor. It can pause or mute itself when a window is maximized, apply a blurred video frame as the GNOME static wallpaper, and restore your original background on exit.

ul.li: Performance, Balanced and Power saving playback profiles
Optional pause on battery and battery status in Settings
Power saving reduces decoder threads, scaling and frame rate
Assign a collection to each monitor
Rotate in order or randomly on a configurable interval
Rotation settings on the Settings page
Favorites, recent wallpapers and collections
Catalogue sorting and resolution filters
Size, duration and resolution on catalogue cards
Flatpak manifest and testing matrix
Playback, wallpaper, language and autostart grouped on one page
Settings reachable from the sidebar, header gear and Home
Configuration, About and Quit actions moved next to the settings
Home page with the current wallpaper and playback state
Monitor cards with resolution, source and playback state
Assign a local video to a single monitor from the Home page
Automatic player restart with capped backoff and a give-up limit
Crash-safe configuration with an automatic backup
WebKit load-error reporting and one automatic retry
Static wallpaper frames are generated off the UI thread
Timeouts for external tools and CI/release automation
Russian interface
Language selector for System, English, Russian and Japanese
Browse live wallpapers with categories, search and pagination
Preview a still and six frames before installing
Download cache with age and size limits
Local, streaming and web-page wallpapers
Multi-monitor support with per-monitor sources
GNOME static wallpaper with blurred video frame
Pause/mute on maximized or fullscreen windows, screen lock and logout handling
Tray icon, autostart, D-Bus API and single-instance handling
